subject: Aurora Health RFP - commercial scenarios: annualized anchoring & graceband options
messages:
From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@aurorahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com, James Kim <james.kim@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora RFP - commercial/pricing clarifications

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking our RFP — a couple of clarifying questions on the commercial section before we schedule a follow-up:

1) We asked for an annualized commit and a monthly rolling commit scenario. Can you provide a worked example (numbers) for both: baseline token price, committed token buckets, and the overage mechanics (rate, graceband, and crediting)?

2) How do you handle transient bursts that exceed a monthly commit by 20-50%? Do you offer a burst cushion, pooled credits, or automatic smoothing? We need the invoice impact explained (how it shows up on month-end invoices).

3) True-up cadence: we typically expect 30-day true-ups but open to proposal. Please specify timing for invoice adjustments and any amortization option for large surges.

4) For multi-year deals, do you offer an acceleration discount (prepay/accelerator) or rate protection? If so, give the trigger examples.

5) Please attach any sample amortization schedules or worked pricing scenarios so our procurement/legal team can review.

Attached: Aurora_RFP_Commercial_Section.pdf (section we filled out).

Appreciate a written reply with worked numbers and we can set a 30-min call next week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Ellis
Sr. Procurement Manager, Aurora Health
procurement@aurorahealth.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: James Kim <james.kim@aurorahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - commercial/pricing clarifications

Sarah — thanks, and great questions. Below is a concise set of worked scenarios and the mechanics we recommend for Aurora given a multi-product deployment (mix of chat generation + embeddings). I've attached a spreadsheet with line-item math (redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx).

Quick context: target steady-state token consumption per month = 1.2B tokens (expected year 1). Your QPS profile shows regular peaks during business hours and occasional one-off campaign-driven surges.

Scenario A — Annualized Anchored Commit (recommended for predictability):
- Annual commit: 14.4B tokens (equivalent to 1.2B/mo anchored)
- Committed unit price (generation tokens): $0.0020 / 1K tokens (baseline)
- Overage price: 1.6x committed rate => $0.0032 / 1K tokens
- Graceband: first 10% over monthly pro rata allocate to burst cushion at 50% of overage rate (i.e., $0.0016 / 1K) and not invoiced until true-up; amounts in cushion are credited back at true-up if unused
- True-up cadence: monthly usage reporting + 30-day reconciliation; annual true-up settlement with invoice credit/debit applied to following invoice
- Amortization option: for any monthly overage > 25% we can amortize excess charge over next 3 months (customer opt-in) to smooth budget impact

Scenario B — Monthly Rolling Commit (recommended for volatile workloads):
- Monthly commit: set to anticipated month x 1.0 (start with 1.2B)
- Committed unit price: $0.0022 / 1K tokens (slightly higher to offset variability)
- Overage price: 1.4x committed rate => $0.00308 / 1K tokens
- Burst handling: automatic burst cushion up to 20% for any single day; anything beyond is billed as overage but eligible for single-month invoice credit if average monthly deviation <10% over a 90-day window

Examples (worked numbers in attached sheet): month with 1.5B tokens under Scenario A -> 300M overage, 10% of monthly pro rata (120M) falls into graceband at discounted cushion rate, true-up will bill remaining 180M at $0.0032/k (unless amortized).

Discounting and multi-year protection:
- 12-month commit: baseline discounts of 5% on committed unit price; 24-month commit: 10%; 36+ months: 12% plus guaranteed rate protection (cap on annual price increases 0-3% depending on CPI clause)
- Acceleration/prepay: customers prefunding >6 months receive additional 2% effective discount on committed price

Next steps: I propose a short call to confirm which scenario Aurora prefers and finalize numbers by deal team (Marissa and Ben are on cc to align on margin and legal terms). If acceptable, we'll produce a formal commercial schedule and a redlineable term sheet.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Commercial | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Aurora RFP - commercial/pricing clarifications

Forwarding Aurora's questions + my draft scenarios. Need quick alignment on: 1) committed price bands (I used $0.0020/1K baseline), 2) graceband mechanics and amortization cap (3 months), and 3) approval for 12/24/36 month tier discounts.

Please review the attached spreadsheet and reply with redline numbers. Margin target for this deal is ~48% blended after discounts; if you see room to be more aggressive for 36+ month, suggest a single small concession on amortization length (4 months) not price.

--Sean

Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurora RFP - commercial/pricing clarifications

Agree with the structure but recommend the following adjustments to protect margin and simplify procurement review:

1) Lower baseline committed price to $0.00195 / 1K tokens for 12-month anchor (we can show as a 2.5% promotional concession).
2) Keep 24-month at 10% off baseline and 36-month at 13% off baseline (one extra point vs draft).
3) Graceband: maintain 10% monthly cushion but convert cushion to pre-funded burst credits that only convert to invoices on repeated use (2+ months in a quarter) — easier for bookkeeping.
4) Amortization: stick to 3 months max; for anything > 50% monthly overage require PO amendment (manual review).

Ben — confirm these look acceptable from finance and whether we can offer an additional 1% concession for public-sector variant if Aurora requires that for procurement.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - commercial/pricing clarifications (formal scenarios)

Sarah — following internal alignment, please find our recommended commercial options for Aurora. I've attached a short proposal (Redwood_Aurora_Commercial_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a worked spreadsheet. Key points below so your procurement/legal team can review quickly:

Option 1 — Annualized Anchor (recommended if Aurora wants predictable unit economics)
- Annual commit: 14.4B tokens (1.2B/mo)
- Committed unit price: $0.00195 / 1K tokens (12-month rate)
- Overage: 1.6x committed => $0.00312 / 1K tokens
- Graceband: 10% monthly cushion implemented as pre-funded burst credits; unused portion carries to next month and is reconciled at 30-day true-up; repeated use (2+ months in a quarter) converts cushion consumption to invoiceable overage at the overage rate unless customer approves amortization
- Amortization: customer may elect to amortize any single-month overage >25% over next 3 months (opt-in)
- Discounts: 24-month = additional 10% off baseline; 36-month = additional 13% off baseline; prepay 6+ months = extra 2%


Option 2 — Monthly Rolling Commit (for variable workloads)
- Monthly commit set at negotiated monthly forecast; committed unit price: $0.00215 / 1K tokens
- Overage: 1.4x committed => $0.00301 / 1K tokens
- Burst cushion: automatic day-level cushion up to 20% for single-day spikes; eligibility for monthly invoice credit if 90-day rolling deviation <10%


Operational notes:
- True-up cadence: monthly reporting + 30-day reconciliation; annual settlement and a single annual invoice credit/debit run for accrual clarity
- Billing representation: invoices will show committed consumption, cushion consumption (separate line as pre-funded credit usage), and any amortized spread (if chosen) so finance can map to budget lines
- Security/compliance: we will include SOC2 Type II evidence and can add audit access for usage logs on request (see Drive link).


If this matches procurement expectations, we can deliver a redlineable commercial schedule and a DocuSign envelope for signature. Proposed next step: 30-min call Wed 3/31 to confirm option selection and finalize terms.


Thanks again — happy to clarify any line items.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Commercial | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
